result.summary: Implemented the design exactly: a cleanup_tmp_dir() function (captures $? as its first statement, removes tmp_dir only when exit_code -eq 0 and TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS is unset, otherwise prints a stderr note preserving it) defined immediately above the existing `tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d ...)` line (former line 245), with `trap cleanup_tmp_dir EXIT` registered on the line immediately after tmp_dir is assigned -- covering all four exit paths (former lines 251, 268, 291, 455) with a single registration, per the design's disposition table. Also added a TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS knob line to the top-of-file comment block (design's OQ-2, left to my discretion) documenting default/semantics. No other lines touched. Verification: `bash -n scripts/test_parallel.sh` passes (syntax check only). A real double-run was not possible in this environment -- this session has Elixir/mix (/c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix) but no local Postgres (`which psql` found none), and the script requires a live Postgres to reach ecto.create/migrate; also this is a Windows dev host while the script itself documents bash/Linux as its target runtime. Verified instead by direct reasoning against the design's disposition table: exit 251/268/291 are unconditional `exit 1` after tmp_dir creation -> exit_code=1 -> trap's else branch preserves tmp_dir (268/291 keep their $tmp_dir/create-$i.log citations valid, matching ISSUE-FIXER's load-bearing requirement); exit 455 with any_failed=0 -> exit_code=0, TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS unset by default -> tmp_dir removed; exit 455 with any_failed=1 -> exit_code=1 -> preserved. Setting TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS to any non-empty value forces preservation even on the exit-0 path, per the `[ -z ... ]` check. set -u is unaffected (both reads use ${VAR:-} or a local always-assigned before use).
